title: The approximation threshold for metric k-median
main_claim: For every fixed ε>0 there is a deterministic polynomial-time (1+2/e+ε)-approximation for metric k-median with candidate facilities. The route: grid preparation (mass ≤ LP+3g, cost ≤ (1+η)LP), then tapered iterative rounding with potential f=aV+(1-y)b, a=A(x)+B(x)(y-x), f0=(1+2/e)V0, giving k+O(1) facilities. Derandomization uses moment-preserving Carathéodory compression, and Li–Svensson removes the additive surplus. Together with the Feige/Max-k-Coverage hardness, the threshold is 1+2/e under P≠NP.

issues.description: I did not re-run the exact rational polynomial certificates. I checked all five scalar bounds numerically instead: dense grids over (x,w,s,r/q) plus Nelder–Mead minimization. Bound (4.4), the first one, is tight: at x=1, w=0, r→0 the two sides meet in the limit, since 1-P(1)=2/e=A(1)-1. It still holds for r>0. This is the expected tightness at the threshold, not a failure. Every other bound has a positive margin (smallest ≈1.2e-3, for the type-zero bound). An exact check of the appendix tables would finish the verification.
issues.evidence: Numerical minima: first(s=0) → 0+ at the boundary only; first(s=1) 0.070; L,charge ≥ 0 (zero at x=0,w=0,r=0); K ≥ 0.306; K-d_sG ≥ 0.019; type-zero ≥ 0.0012; type-one ≥ 0.056.

coverage: Read every section. Checked by hand the generator expansion (Lemma 5.5), the coefficient identity (1+y)a+yB+x(y-x)B'-1=3y+B(y-x)^2, and that the normalized expression equals the left side of Theorem 4.1 exactly. Also checked the time derivative ḟ=-x(y-x)B'V, the cap-split bound, the kernel bound, and the radius-replacement error 12ζ. Checked the forced-case savings (Y≥δb', savings ≥ BgV), terminal correction, survival bound, and count lemma (linear expectation, Efron–Stein/Chebyshev scaling, independence from b_*). Checked the preparation budget (+3g identity and exceptional-star error <2), far/near cost comparisons, the Theorem 6.4 loss arithmetic, and the moment requirements for derandomization (pair edge moments, degree-4 trigger moments, conflict-filter bounds). Verified analytic identities with scipy, verified Lemma 4.2 numerically, and ran an adversarial hill-climbing search (4000 restarts, n≤5) on Theorem 4.1 with R_i at its maximal admissible value: no violation, supremum ≈ -1.6e-5. Did not re-derive the exact rational certificates in the appendix, and did not independently check the external Li–Svensson reduction beyond its stated interface.
